question.leadin: One succession conflict in this empire saw Huascar executed by Atahualpa, who became Huayna Capac's successor.
question.text: Name this Realm of Four Parts centered on the city of Cusco. This Andean empire was founded by Pachacuti.
question.clue: A civil war in this empire was won by a son born outside its royal family, and who allegedly ordered the execution of his brother.

swap.leadin: Tupac Amaru's 1572 uprising could not reverse the fate of this empire.
swap.text: Identify this empire that was weakened by the civil war between the sons of Huayna Capac.
swap.clue: One ruler of these people allegedly gained a fortune from places termed the "Outer Belt" and the "Fire Belt," and another earned a name meaning "overturner of the world" or "earthshaker" after stones supposedly came to life to help him repel Chanka invaders.

question.leadin: Like the related Aymaras, the women of this ethnic group often wear bowler hats.
question.text: Identify this ethnic group that is indigenous to the Andes. The language of this ethnic group was used by the Incans to record messages on quipus.
question.answerHtml: Quechua [accept more specific groups such as Runakuna, Kichwas, or Ingas]
question.clue: The MUPP-NP party's common name is a word in this language that's gained popularity with indigenists for its connotation of "world reversal."

swap.text: Timur allegedly built pyramids out of these body parts, the protective structure for the brain, which would terrify his enemies.
swap.clue: After sacking Ankara in Turkey, Tamerlane allegedly made a pyramid of these objects.

question.leadin: Women new to this city were sent to schools called acllahuasi ("ock-yah-WAH-see"), where they were trained to become secluded virgins who brewed chicha.
question.text: Name this former capital that was shaped like a jaguar and built from stone without using mortar. This capital surrendered after Atalhualpa was captured at Cajamarca.
question.clue: A chief of this puma-shaped city adopted a name roughly translated as "world turner."

swap.leadin: Name some things about the downfall of the Incan Empire.
swap.text: The downfall of the Incan empire began when Pizarro launched this surprise attack on the royal Incan family. Pizarro's capture of the Inca here led to him demanding a room full of gold as ransom.
swap.clue: The losing side in this battle was engaged in a civil war against Huascar and was crippled by the decision to leave the bulk of its army outside the city walls.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Andean civilizations.
question.text: This culture existed in the Ica river valley succeeding the Paracas culture. These people are famous for theirnamesake lines which form geoglyphs visible from the sky.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about a certain precious metal in pre-Columbian South America.
swap.text: One of the leaders of this confederation ritually covered himself in gold dust before diving into Lake Guatavita. This confederation, which was led by a Zipa and a Zaque ["ZAH-kay"], held territory in the highlands of modern-day Colombia.
swap.clue: Perhaps this polity's most well-known artefact is known as this polity's "raft", which is a gold sculpture that was found in Lake Guatavita.

question.leadin: The execution of Antonio de Arriaga instigated a rebellion led by a man with this regnal name.
question.text: Give this two-word name of an indigenous Peruvian rebel leader who claimed descent from the final Sapa Inca. That Neo-Incan ruler with this regnal name was executed by the Spanish in 1572.
question.clue: The legitimate son of Manco Capac, he was captured an executed for the death of Friar Diego Ortiz.

swap.leadin: A first-year undergrad named Manny Medrano helped decode a system used in these things.
swap.text: Identify these records made from alpaca and llama fibers, most commonly used for keeping track of tribute.
swap.clue: The coarsest wool was instead woven by commoners and used to make chusi, a cloth used for ch'uspa sacks and blankets, or the knotted cords that comprise these recordkeeping devices.

question.text: This Inca city was shaped like a puma and served as the capital of the empire. Legend holds that it was built by Pachacuti.
question.clue: A man who claimed to be a direct descendant of that son two centuries later staged an indigenous uprising before being executed in this city.

swap.text: Incan relay messengers, the chasquis, carried messages via these "talking knots" that were made of llama hair.
swap.clue: This objects that were used for record-keeping and other purposes by the Inca.

question.text: Vilcabamba was founded by this Incan monarch. This monarch was captured by Spanish forces and imprisoned by the brothers of Francisco Pizarro before escaping and laying siege to Cusco for 10 months.

swap.text: The Incan empire used this system of taxation, in which males over the age of 15 were required to provide labor for construction projects.
swap.clue: A revival of this system that ignored traditional boundaries was created by Francisco de Toledo to support the new mining town of Huancavelica.

question.leadin: These people invented one of the first medium distance communication systems with two resin-coated gourds connected by a 75m length of twine.
question.text: Name these people who had their capital at Chan Chan and who made use of the Spondylus shellfish and produced notably black shiny pottery.
question.clue: These people succeeded the Moche, and they ruled from their capital at Chan Chan.

swap.leadin: After being attacked by the rival Chanka people, this ruler is said to have called on the sun god Inti to turn stones into pururauca warriors to defend his city.
swap.text: Name this son of Viracocha who transformed the Kingdom of Cuzco into the Incan Empire in the 15th century.
swap.clue: This king commissioned life-sized gold statues of animals and plant for the central garden of his Coricancha temple.

question.text: Further south, warfare with the Incas would certainly involve facing this prestigious general, who defeated Huascar at Quipaipan before losing to the Spanish at Vilcaconga and Maraycalla. He was killed by a mutiny in 1534 afer attempting to build resistance against Spain from a mountain stronghold.
question.clue: A man with this name failed to capture the town of Jauja from the Spanish shortly after being defeated by them at the Battle of Cusco.

swap.leadin: This cloud forest culture created mosaic friezes at Gran Pajaten ("pa-ha-TEN"), built cliff tombs at Revash, and produced the Laguna de Los Condores textiles.
swap.text: Name this culture that built the walled city of Kuelap in Amazonas, Peru. This culture's people were ascribed white skin by Inca chroniclers, whose reports of their ferocity inspired their nickname of "warriors of the clouds."

question.leadin: This system was instituted by the Spanish in 1573 to draft people to work the mines of Potosi.
question.text: Identify this form of labor tax which used by the Incans for such infrastructure projects as the construction of the extensive network of roads.
question.clue: Las Casas would likely not have approved of the Spanish adoption of this Incan labor system which allowed them to conscript natives for public service work.

swap.leadin: Along with the Chavin culture, this culture was investigated by Julio Tello, who found hundreds of "mummy bundles" on a peninsula that shares this culture's name.
swap.text: Name this culture that built a necropolis at its site of Wari Kayan. This Andean culture in modern-day Peru strongly influenced its successor, the Nazca culture.
